--- title: "Uncertainty Decomposition: Aleatoric vs. Epistemic" description: "Decompose prediction uncertainty into aleatoric (data noise) and epistemic (model) components using bootstrap ensembles." date: today format: html: self-contained: true embed-resources: true code-fold: true code-tools: true --- Not all uncertainty is equal. This notebook decomposes prediction uncertainty into: - **Aleatoric uncertainty** — irreducible noise in the data (e.g., measurement error) - **Epistemic uncertainty** — reducible uncertainty from limited data or model capacity We use the `EnsembleDecomposition` class with bootstrap refitting to quantify each component on the **synthetic heteroscedastic** dataset (where noise varies with input features). ::: {#setup .cell cache='true' execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import polars as pl from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingRegressor from uncertainty_flow.decomposition import EnsembleDecomposition from uncertainty_flow.wrappers import ConformalRegressor ``` ::: ::: {#cell-load-data .cell cache='true' execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pl.read_parquet("../data/synthetic_heteroscedastic.parquet") print(f"Shape: {df.shape}") df.head(10) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Shape: (5000, 7) ``` ::: ::: {#load-data .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#decomposition .cell cache='true' execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} n_bootstrap = 10 confidence = 0.9 sample_size = 500 n = df.height split_idx = int(n * 0.7) train_df = df[:split_idx] eval_df = df[split_idx:] eval_sample = eval_df.sample(n=min(sample_size, eval_df.height), seed=42) def model_factory(): return ConformalRegressor( base_model=GradientBoostingRegressor(random_state=42), auto_tune=False, random_state=42, ) decomp = EnsembleDecomposition( model_factory=model_factory, train_data=train_df, target="y", confidence=confidence, n_bootstrap=n_bootstrap, random_state=42, ) overall, by_sample = decomp.decompose(eval_sample), decomp.decompose_by_sample(eval_sample) print("Decomposition complete") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` /Users/minghao/Desktop/personal/uncertainty_flow/uncertainty_flow/wrappers/conformal.py:237: UncertaintyFlowWarning: Residual correlation analysis found no significant drivers.
